page: Amazon Web Services c6id.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base frequency of 3.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, and a 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. No GPU resources are available on this instance type, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1888.1 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1600.0. However, multi-core and memory performance represent significant bottlenecks. The stress-ng multi-core score is weak at 3863.16, and the Passmark memory score is poor at 1060.81. Memory bandwidth is limited, yielding 29.55 GB/sec for large block reads and 24.58 GB/sec for large block writes. For file operations, single-threaded gzip compression reaches 28.1 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput is moderate at 6.41 GB/sec.

The c6id.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require high-frequency single-core execution paired with fast local scratch space, avoiding the latency and cost of network-attached storage. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and weak multi-threaded scaling. This instance is best suited for single-threaded compute tasks, lightweight web serving, and applications requiring temporary local NVMe storage with a minimal memory footprint.
